independence_declaration.statement: I (code-security-reviewer) authored none of the implementation in the reviewed scope. I formed this verdict before reading any other round-18 review record, and read none. All code execution ran in disposable clones and fixtures inside this run's private $TMPDIR. No reproduction touched another agent's files, scratch or processes; the live concurrent peer runs were deliberately not probed. No /proc/sys or other host tunable was written (mode-bit reads only).

checks_run.procedure: Confirm the frozen candidate: HEAD is a metadata-only commit after the freeze; recompute the candidate ID from the working tree and from a clone at the frozen commit
checks_run.command: git rev-parse HEAD; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0; git diff --name-only 450c756..HEAD; (clone) git checkout 450c756 && node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG0
checks_run.environment: agent shell (Claude Code Bash sandbox inside the D-030 process sandbox), node v22.22.2
checks_run.expected: candidate_id sha256:21efe44b...023cc5; post-freeze commits touch only excluded metadata
checks_run.actual: HEAD ccb989f (metadata-only: assignments, candidate manifest, stages.json); candidate_id sha256:21efe44b6a4613a004b27282e66db59d42254903e5e2c6e2d0a8398a5e023cc5 from both the working tree and the clone at 450c756 (90 files)

checks_run.procedure: Review the full code diff since the round-17 candidate plus the full touched file (agent_sandbox.py)
checks_run.expected: Only the D-032 changes (finish() FileExistsError handling, docstring, one test)
checks_run.actual: Only tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py (+12/-3) and tools/agents/tests/process-sandbox.test.mjs (+20). CI, gates, guard and agent definitions are unchanged since round 17.

checks_run.procedure: Run the gate and agent test suites in a clone at the candidate commit
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 450c756 under $TMPDIR; nested bwrap 0.9.0 available

checks_run.procedure: Run the pre-freeze checks in a fresh clone of the candidate commit
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 450c756 under $TMPDIR; checks run sandboxed via tools/gates/sandbox-run.sh
checks_run.actual: 11/11 PASS (source extraction reproducible, validator+guard tests, runner tests, register rules, register merge, pipeline, 4 analysis checks, working-tree candidate equals HEAD 21efe44b...)

checks_run.procedure: Check whether one process-sandboxed run can write into another concurrently running run's areas via /proc/<peer-pid>/root or /cwd (residuals 7/8). Uses two sibling sandboxes built from the REAL agent_sandbox.py args in a throwaway fixture; the attacker runs at the process-sandbox layer with the file tools' credentials
checks_run.environment: agent shell; nested bwrap inside the Claude Code Bash sandbox (analogue of the live topology; live peer runs not probed)
checks_run.expected: every write into the peer's evidence, TMPDIR, staging and session directory is refused, as threat-model row 2 and residuals 7/8 state
checks_run.actual: Direct write refused (Read-only file system), but writes via /proc/<peer>/root and /cwd succeed into the peer's evidence, private TMPDIR, staged review record and session directory, including via a symlink in the attacker's own evidence dir. The peer's finish() then copies the forged record back as its own (exit 0, discarded=[]). Finding F-DG0-152.

checks_run.procedure: Spike a narrower mitigation for C5: a scope-only Landlock domain per run (handled_access_fs=0, scoped=SIGNAL|ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET), and confirm that the nested fresh-procfs bwrap still works
checks_run.environment: agent shell; kernel 6.18.44, Landlock ABI 7; throwaway fixture
checks_run.expected: cross-run /proc writes and signals refused; own areas writable; nested bwrap --proc works
checks_run.actual: Without Landlock: cross-run writes succeed and signal allowed. With Landlock: /proc/<peer>/root and /cwd writes 'Permission denied', signal 'Operation not permitted', own evidence and TMPDIR writable, nested bwrap with fresh --proc works.

checks_run.procedure: Verify F-DG0-150 against the old and new code, and confirm that the D-031 concurrency fix, --unshare-ipc (F-DG0-148) and F-DG0-147 still behave as before (round-17 reproduction re-run on both trees)
checks_run.environment: git archive of tools/agents at each commit under $TMPDIR; throwaway fixtures
checks_run.expected: old: case D exits 1 with FileExistsError; new: case D exits 3 with a write-once discard; A, B, C, E unchanged
checks_run.actual: old: D exit=1 FileExistsError, no sandbox.json; new: D exit=3, discarded 'already present in the real tree; write-once', real file kept. A: private ipc ns on both. B: exit 0, no false discard. C: scope discards unchanged. E: backdated own-role file still copied back (F-DG0-147).

checks_run.procedure: F-DG0-150 fix edge cases: the loop continues after a collision; a planted dest symlink is not followed
checks_run.expected: new code: exit 3, collision and symlink discarded, later file copied back, symlink target not created
checks_run.actual: old: exit 1, sandbox.json missing, b.json not copied. new: exit 3, a.json and c.json discarded, b.json copied back, symlink not followed.

checks_run.procedure: F-DG0-149 read-only assessment: the CLI process's credentials (Read tool on /proc/self/status), the mount configuration in source, a test -w mode-bit read; no /proc/sys write
checks_run.command: Read /proc/self/status (CLI file-tool layer); grep of agent_sandbox.py bwrap_args; test -w /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern inside the fixture sandbox
checks_run.environment: live CLI process (own process only); throwaway fixture sandbox
checks_run.actual: The CLI runs in the host PID namespace (pid 2552), uid 0, all capability sets = 0x80000000 (CAP_SETFCAP), NoNewPrivs 1, Seccomp 0. /proc is a host rw bind with no /proc/sys submount, and core_pattern reports writable (mode bits only). The residual is larger than disclosed because of C5 (F-DG0-152); F-DG0-149 is kept OPEN.

checks_run.procedure: CI workflow least privilege, pinning, fetch depth and failure propagation; credential-pattern scan of tracked files
checks_run.command: grep of .github/workflows/delivery-gates.yml; git ls-files | xargs grep -E '<AWS/Anthropic/GitHub/Slack key, private key, password literal patterns>'
checks_run.expected: contents: read; SHA-pinned actions; fetch-depth 0; no continue-on-error; no secrets
checks_run.actual: permissions contents: read; actions/checkout and setup-node pinned by SHA; fetch-depth 0; validator --pipeline/--reconcile steps without continue-on-error; no secrets.* use; zero credential-pattern matches

checks_run.procedure: F-DG0-151: compare the module docstring, bwrap_args, sandbox.json fields and threat-model.md wording
checks_run.expected: all descriptions consistent with --unshare-ipc and a shared PID namespace
checks_run.actual: The docstring is now correct (F-DG0-151 fixed). threat-model.md:27 still says 'creates no PID/IPC namespace of its own' (F-DG0-153, Low).

summary: FAIL. The D-032 fixes hold: F-DG0-150 and F-DG0-151 are CLOSED_VERIFIED; D-031 and --unshare-ipc still hold; F-DG0-147 is re-accepted as an observation. Tests (91/91) and the pre-freeze (11/11) pass, and CI and the secrets scan are clean. New High finding F-DG0-152: the host-bind procfs plus the shared PID namespace let a process at the sandbox layer write into a concurrent run's evidence, clones, staged record and session directory via /proc/<peer-pid>/root. This was reproduced with the real sandbox args in a disposable fixture; a scope-only Landlock domain per run closes it in a spike. F-DG0-149 therefore stays OPEN, because residual 7 is larger than disclosed. New Low F-DG0-153: stale threat-model wording.
